StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterModifyingCardPlayCount.rationale: C# consumes the stack from a separate after-hook (DuplicationPower.cs:27-30 -> PowerCmd.Decrement) that Hook.ModifyCardPlayCount fires immediately after the modifier chain and before the plays resolve (Hook.cs:1372-1384, one of the ten modifier-notification lists hook_dispatch step 38 enumerates). The sim folds the decrement into the modifier itself. Equivalent today, for the reason the sim's own docstring gives, and Duplication always changes the count so it is always in C#'s notification list. Kept as a divergence rather than faithful because the sim has no notification machinery at all -- the same absence as audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G4 one family over -- so a second play-count listener that only sometimes changes the count could not be expressed. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the player-side leg moved off the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (`on_player_turn_end`) onto `after_player_turn_end`, which combat.py:809 dispatches AFTER `_process_turn_end_cards` and the hand flush -- the sim's port of Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading combat.py:781-812 and this power's class in powers.py. WAS: the effect ran inside Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, so its order relative to the turn-end card effects, the flush and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays was hook registration order. The registration-order witness is doubly gone: StampedePower also moved, to `after_auto_post_play_phase_entered` (powers.py:1089), which combat.py:789 fires strictly before this slot.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3922-3926 reduces this to `self.owner is combat.player`, and the sim's own comment explains why: one player, every card belongs to it. Same reading as power_cmd's sim-entry note.

C# doubles any card type; powers.py:3919-3928 likewise applies no type test. Contrast power/one_two_punch, whose C# file DOES restrict to Attacks and whose sim port restricts too -- the pair is correct in both directions.
Duplication overrides no AfterRemoved, so the observable is identical; _expire (powers.py:86-92) bypasses RemoveInternal/AfterRemoved. Same note as power/no_draw's.
